notes: The Flight Deck Suite mission patch is the Manager's new logo: in the window, the taskbar, the notification area and the Start menu.
Each app's card and row shows its own badge, the patch's frame with the app's symbol.
Running the setup file opens a setup window with the patch: it asks before installing and shows the install's progress.
About shows the trademark line under the credit.

Running the setup file opens a setup window with the patch: it asks before installing and shows the install's progress.
About shows the trademark line under the credit.
Each app's Details page names every folder on this PC, such as Your flights, Playback recordings, Video clips and Screenshots, with a note on what's in it.
How much space each folder takes, shown beside its name.
Folder paths wrap neatly between folder names, and the Open buttons line up.
Settings › Folders also lists the Manager's own folder, with a note on each.
Tidier layouts: every update shows its version and date, and badges and buttons sit evenly in a narrow window.
Update alerts: the Manager can start with Windows, wait beside the clock and show a notification when an update is ready, never while MSFS is running. It asks once; Settings switches it on or off.
Every update lists all of its changes, and each app's Details page has its version history.
Update all, when more than one update is ready.
Repair, on an app's Details page: installs the same version afresh. Settings and data stay as they are.
The app cards come first, and Finish setting up folds away to one line once everything is set up.
Start with MSFS moved to Settings; each app's card says when it opens with the sim.
A Help page: the common fixes, Copy details for support, the guides and What's new.
The Terms of Use, Privacy Policy and third-party notices can be read on the About page.
On this PC, in each app's Details: the real folders with Open buttons, and the copy kept by Take over can be deleted.
Logbook's Details page points to Move to a new PC, for taking your flights to another computer.

Take over: an app installed by hand (before the Manager) can be handed to the Manager, which then updates it. Its settings and data stay where they are, and the copy installed by hand is kept as a backup.
The first public release.

apps.name: Logbook
apps.desc: Logs every flight by itself, with an accurate landing rate, landing replays, the Logbook site and Share my flight.
notes: Route maps have a Full screen button: the map alone on the whole screen, with Esc or the same button to come back. The Show all button has its own icon, so the two can't be confused.

apps.name: Ramp
apps.desc: Parks airliners on empty stands in the right airlines for each airport, and keeps your gate and VATSIM pilots' stands clear.
notes: Parked aircraft no longer vanish as you taxi past them; only the gate you park on or really pull into is cleared, and the aircraft beside your gate stay unless your wings would reach them.
